title: SKCapstone ITIL record core (incident / problem / change)
description: Derived from all 304 incidents, 3 problems and 11 changes in ~/.skcapstone/coordination/itil as of 2026-08-27. core.json holds IMMUTABLE creation facts only. Current state is NOT stored here: it is derived from the events log. See itil-event.v1.schema.json.

id.description: Prefix encodes the record type and MUST agree with the type field. All 318 observed ids are exactly 12 chars: a 3-char prefix, a hyphen, and 8 lowercase hex.

severity_at_creation.description: Named _at_creation on purpose: severity may be revised later via an event, and this field must never be rewritten.

dedup_key.description: <ci_identity>:<condition>. REQUIRED for any machine-generated record. Dedup is only as good as this key: if the CI identity embeds a volatile token, dedup silently fails and a fresh record is minted on every restart. See CMDB-IDENT-01. 7 of 318 live records omit it entirely, all manually created; it is required for machine-generated records and should become required for all.

ci_identity.description: STABLE identity only. TWO defect classes were found in live data and this pattern deliberately rejects both, so current violations are the remediation backlog, not a reason to loosen the schema. (1) Machine-generated identities embedding a process id, e.g. ci-service-sklegal-s102-3620007-4e13b305: 122 of 263 drift incidents, 118 for one service, every restart minting a permanent new incident. (2) Manually created records using free-text service names with spaces and parentheses, e.g. 'skgraph (FalkorDB)' and 'skchat daemon': about 30 records, which also corrupts the derived dedup_key. See CMDB-IDENT-01.
